subtitle: Ring Modulator
tagline: A four-control ring modulator with an internal carrier from 0.1 Hz to 5 kHz, moving from slow tremolo to metallic sidebands.

body.lead: TB Ring Modulation multiplies the input by an internal carrier. At low carrier frequencies this sounds like tremolo and pulsing amplitude; at higher frequencies it creates new, often metallic sidebands above and below the original sound.

body.p: Four controls cover it: `FREQUENCY` sets the carrier, `SHAPE` morphs its waveform, `TONE` focuses the top end of the modulated signal, and `MIX` places the effect. Parameter and bypass smoothing keep automation clean on mono or stereo sources, and no external routing is needed.

ul: Internal carrier from 0.1 Hz to 5 kHz
SHAPE morphs from sine through triangle to square
TONE low-pass on the modulated signal
MIX blends the dry and ring-modulated signals
Carrier field display with frequency, shape, and waveform
6 factory presets, user presets, undo, and redo

note.title: About this manual
text: This manual describes TB Ring Modulation 1.0.0 for Windows (VST3). The current macOS build is also version 1.0.0; small differences between platforms are possible.

ol: Insert TB Ring Modulation on a vocal, drum, synth, or guitar track. The defaults are `FREQUENCY` 120 Hz, `SHAPE` sine, `TONE` 12 kHz, and `MIX` 50%.
For tremolo, set `FREQUENCY` {{3}} below about 20 Hz.
For metallic or robotic tones, raise `FREQUENCY` into the hundreds or thousands of hertz.
Make the carrier harsher with `SHAPE` {{4}}, and tame the top end with `TONE` {{5}}.

rows: The internal carrier frequency. Low values give tremolo and pulsing; high values give inharmonic, metallic sidebands.
Morphs the carrier from sine (0%) through triangle (50%) to square (100%). Toward square there are more harmonics, so check the high end.
Low-pass cutoff on the ring-modulated signal. It does not change the carrier frequency.
Blends the dry and ring-modulated signals. At 100% the original pitch cues change strongly.
Bypasses the complete effect, with smoothing.

tip.text: Ring modulation sounds most musical when the carrier is related to the key, for example the root or the fifth. Unrelated frequencies give clangorous, bell-like or robotic results.

body.p: Step through presets with the arrows; hold an arrow to browse continuously. Open the list to choose a factory or user preset. Save stores the current settings as a .tbring file. Undo and Redo step through recent changes. The factory presets can also be selected from the host through a program parameter.
Starting points for common jobs. Adjust them by ear.

recipes.title: Tremolo
recipes.use: A gentle amplitude pulse on guitar or keys.
steps: Set FREQUENCY to taste; it is free-running, not tempo-synced.

recipes.title: Robot voice
steps: Lower TONE if the buzz is too harsh.

recipes.title: Bell and metal textures
recipes.use: Clangorous tones on percussion or synths.
steps: Sweep FREQUENCY slowly to find pleasing sidebands.

recipes.title: Lo-fi radio
steps: Combine with a high-pass EQ for a smaller sound.

rows: Lower TONE, move SHAPE toward sine, or lower MIX.
The pitch of the source disappears.
That is normal at high MIX and FREQUENCY. Lower MIX to keep the original pitch audible.
Low frequencies sound like a pulse, not a tone.
Below about 20 Hz the carrier works like tremolo. Raise FREQUENCY for sidebands.
MIX is at 0% or the effect is bypassed.
